---
title: "Incident 2026-10-02: break-glass"
type: incident
entities: [phoenix, defiant]
changes: [c-b7gl4s]
tags: [break-glass, openbao, sso]
---
# Incident 2026-10-02: break-glass

## Summary

On 2026-10-02 at 07:40 the SSO provider returned errors after a certificate
expired. Nobody could log in to defiant with kubelogin. A tenant job queue
was stuck and needed a node drain. jonas used the break-glass certificate
from OpenBao at 08:05.

## Timeline

| Time | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 07:40 | SSO token endpoint returns 500. kubelogin fails for all admins. |
| 07:55 | Tenant reports stuck jobs on cn-031. |
| 08:05 | jonas reads the break-glass certificate from OpenBao. Alert to all owners and platform admins. |
| 08:12 | cn-031 drained and rebooted. Jobs run again. |
| 09:30 | SSO certificate renewed. kubelogin works. |
| 10:10 | Break-glass certificate rotated in OpenBao. |

## Follow-up

- The SSO certificate now has a renewal alert 14 days before expiry.
- The break-glass use is recorded in the merge commit of c-b7gl4s with the
  trailer `Pk-Break-Glass: openbao-cert 2026-10-02`.

+jb-05 is a Western Digital Ultrastar Data60 shelf with two drawers. In
+`jb-05.yaml` drawers and slots count from 0, as in the enclosure firmware.
+
+| Drawer | Slots | Front label | Linux device order |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 0 (top) | 0 to 23 | A01 to A24 | sda to sdx |
+| 1 (bottom) | 0 to 23 | B01 to B24 | sdy to sdav |
+
+- The front label counts from 1. Slot 17 in drawer 1 is label **B18**.
+- Rows of 6 slots run from the front to the back of the drawer.
+- `sg_ses --page=aes /dev/sg<N>` shows the slot of a device. Device names can
+  change after a reboot; the slot and the serial do not.
+- A blinking amber LED means the operator holds the slot for replacement.

+# Add a compute node to a cluster
+
+A compute node is one file in `control/inventory/`. The bench renders it into
+a `Machine` for its cluster, and the metal operator installs Talos on it.
+
+## Steps
+
+1. Open a change and link the work item:
+
+   ```
+   pk change new "Add cn-035 to defiant" --intent "compute node for tenants" --work-item w-114
+   ```
+
+2. Add the node from kind **Node** (Files, New file). Set the cluster, the
+   role and the rack location. A 2U node at unit 6 fills units 6 and 7.
+3. Cable the ports. The form shows the free ports of `mgmt`, `data-a` and
+   `data-b`. Use one port on `data-a` and one on `data-b`, so the node keeps
+   traffic when one data switch fails. The bench checks that each switch port
+   is free and each cable id is unique.
+4. Add the node to the BGP peering policy of its rack
+   (`clusters/<cluster>/infra/cilium/bgp-<rack>.yaml`). A node that no policy
+   selects gets no routes. The advisor "Check this commit" finds a missing node.
+5. Run the change lab. The inventory path needs a green lab on the head of
+   the branch. The default scenario installs Talos through the emulated BMC,
+   joins the node, checks BGP and takes `data-b` down.
+6. Mark ready. Two platform admins approve. Merge.
+
+## Checks after merge
+
+- The change shows `deployed` when Flux applied the merge commit on the
+  cluster, and `verified` when the node is Ready and BGP is up.

+---
+# Replace a failed disk in a storage node
+
+Use this runbook when Ceph marks an OSD on sn-05 as down and the disk is in
+jb-05. The desired state of each slot is in `control/inventory/jb-05.yaml`.
+
+## Before you start
+
+- Find the OSD and its device: `ceph osd tree down` and
+  `ceph device ls-by-host sn-05`.
+- Map the device to a drawer and a slot with
+  [JBOD drawers: slot numbers](../hardware/jbod-slot-numbers.md).
+- Check that the cluster is healthy apart from this OSD: `ceph health detail`.
+  Do not start when placement groups are already degraded for another reason.
+
+## Steps
+
+1. Open a change:
+
+   ```
+   pk change new "Replace disk jb-05 slot 17" --intent "OSD down on sn-05, disk in drawer 1 slot 17"
+   ```
+
+2. Set the slot to `replace`:
+
+   ```
+   pk edit jb-05 --set drawers[1].slots[17].state=replace
+   ```
+
+3. Run the change lab, mark the change ready and get one approval.
+4. Merge. The storage operator drains the OSD and marks it out. Wait until
+   `ceph -s` shows no misplaced objects.
+5. Replace the disk. The slot LED blinks amber while the operator holds it.
+6. The asset DB sync opens a change with the new serial. Review it, then set
+   the slot back to `ok` in the same change.
+
+## After the replacement
+
+- Ceph backfills the new OSD. This takes about 6 h for a 20 TB disk.
+- Add a line to the incident log if more than one disk failed in a week.

+---
+# Ceph OSD layout on pegasus
+
+pegasus runs Ceph with Rook. One storage node, sn-05, holds the OSDs of the
+jb-05 disk shelf. The CephCluster is in
+`clusters/pegasus/infra/rook-ceph/cephcluster.yaml`.
+
+## Layout
+
+| Item | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| Storage node | sn-05 (Huawei 2288H V5), GC5A-6Y U20 |
+| Disk shelf | jb-05, 2 drawers with 24 slots each, SAS to sn-05 |
+| OSDs | one OSD per disk, 48 OSDs |
+| Failure domain | `osd` (single node; host failure domain comes with sn-06) |
+| Pools | `rbd-tenants` (replica 3), `cephfs-data` (EC 4+2) |
+
+## Decisions
+
+- One OSD per disk. NVMe for WAL/DB is not in the shelf, so each OSD keeps
+  its own WAL and DB on the spinning disk. Write latency is acceptable for
+  the batch workloads on defiant.
+- The failure domain stays `osd` until a second storage node exists. A host
+  failure takes the pool down; the backups on tape cover this.
+- Slot state lives in git (`jb-05.yaml`). A disk replacement is a normal
+  change, see [Replace a failed disk](../runbooks/replace-failed-disk.md).
